title: Strange food from around the world
text: Every country has its own food, and sometimes the food of other countries looks very strange to us. But remember: your normal food is strange for someone too!
In Iceland, people eat hakarl, a shark that is left for months to dry. It has a very strong smell, and many visitors cannot eat much of it. Locals usually eat a small piece with a drink.
In Japan, natto is a popular breakfast. It is made from beans and it is very sticky. When you lift it with your chopsticks, long threads come with it. A lot of Japanese people eat it with rice.
In Sardinia, an island in Italy, there is a cheese with live insects inside. It is called casu marzu. Some people love it, but it is illegal to sell it in many places.
In Mexico, chapulines are grasshoppers fried with lime and chili. They are crunchy and they have a lot of protein. You can buy many of them at markets, like snacks. Would you try them?
q: What is special about casu marzu?
What do chapulines have a lot of?
halves: It is illegal to sell casu marzu...

grammar.title: Grammar: much, many and a lot of
grammar.rule: Use many with things you can count and much with things you cannot count, mostly in questions and negatives. A lot of works with both.
items: You can buy ___ grasshoppers at markets.

es.title: Comidas raras del mundo
es.sub: Platos que sorprenden a los visitantes
es.grammar: Gramática: much, many y a lot of. Many con cosas que se cuentan; much con cosas que no se cuentan (sobre todo en preguntas y negativas). A lot of vale para las dos.
